claims.text: The reported raspberry MAP study found that a 5% O₂/15% CO₂ atmosphere reduced Botrytis incidence by 63% relative to an ambient-air control and maintained firmness above commercial thresholds for 12 days versus 6 days in air, with sensory marketability at day 10 under optimal MAP.

claims.text: Related work attributed to this researcher screened 12 commercial films differing in OTR and CO₂TR for mixed-berry trays at 2 °C and used finite-element gas-permeation modelling to confirm headspace trends and predict equilibrium under alternative fill weights; one film (OTR 3,800, CO₂TR 18,000 cm³/m²/day) kept headspace within acceptable ranges for three species and cut mould incidence 55% versus a polyethylene control.

limitations: Findings concern pre-cooling protocols at 2 °C experimental scale; applicability to the company's packing-house line is unverified.

Film specification capability: 12-film OTR/CO₂TR screening with finite-element gas-permeation modelling shows a method to convert measured permeability and headspace data into a candidate specification, matching the company's stated need to translate OTR/CO₂TR numbers into a film grade.

Condensation and pre-cooling: evidence on forced-air versus room cooling and hydrocooling links equilibration speed and free moisture to Botrytis incidence, relevant to the company's micro-condensation hypothesis.

Cold-chain data use: existing work ingesting temperature/humidity streams into Botrytis-relevant prediction models indicates usable methodology for FreshPak's two seasons of logs and destination inspection reports.

cooperationScope.text: Scope: a film-specification and trial-design project using FreshPak's lab (OTR/CO₂TR, headspace gas, seal strength) and historic shipment data, with milestones (a) translation of logs into a temperature/humidity profile, (b) modelled headspace and Botrytis risk ranking for a short candidate film list, (c) simulated-transit trial protocol and its execution, (d) pre-season consignment check.
Engagement form to agree: joint project and/or industrial PhD co-supervision, consistent with the researcher's stated openness.

validation.text: Baseline: current lidding film and seal pressure run in the simulated-transit protocol, recording visible Botrytis incidence at days 9 and 14 and headspace O₂/CO₂. Candidate films are measured the same way, with model-predicted versus observed equilibrium gas composition compared per film and fill weight. Go/no-go: advance to the pre-season consignment check only if the best candidate reaches the agreed mould-incidence threshold and its observed headspace trend is consistent with the model; otherwise revise film, seal setting or pre-cooling before the season deadline.

constraints.text: Required inputs from FreshPak: the two current film grades and their measured OTR/CO₂TR, standard punnet geometry and fill weight, seal pressure range, two seasons of temperature/humidity logs and destination inspection reports, and lab time for headspace and seal testing. Engagement is limited to the researcher's lab and part-time involvement; no large external testing programme can be assumed given the stated budget.

What remains outside the supported scope: heat-seal and anti-fog film behaviour, micro-condensation control in the 125 g rPET shell, compostable-material migration, and full commercial deployment or a contractual one-percent mould guarantee.

findings.explanation: R0926 (Sofija Ristić, ranked 3) is a mechanical-engineering sealing-systems researcher whose registered corpus concerns elastomeric gaskets, O-rings and IP-rated electromechanical/enclosure housings: condensation inside sealed electrical enclosures (E014, E072), moisture ingress through compressed gaskets in IP54 steel cabinets (E012), FIP vs EPDM gaskets on electrical cabinets (E094). Her project MOISTMOD targets low-voltage electrical enclosure condensation modelling with a Python prediction tool (E007, E142). There is no registered Evidence of perishable-food, berry, MAP or food-packaging work, and her industry experience is enclosure/cabinet manufacturers (E127). Keyword overlap ('condensation', 'sealed', 'modelling') therefore does not establish technical suitability for Botrytis control in raspberry punnets; her 'modelling' expertise is heat-moisture transfer in non-food cavities, not respiration/permeability-based MAP design.
findings.recheckQuestion: Does R0926 have any registered Evidence of fresh-produce or food-packaging MAP work, as opposed to electromechanical enclosure condensation?

findings.explanation: R0426 (Aleksandar Bošković, ranked 4) contributes injection-moulding thermomechanical simulation: warpage/residual stress in PA6 and PP parts, mould heat-transfer-coefficient calibration and cooling-circuit CFD (E100, E172, E002, E108, E016, E111). His sole condensation-related item is a co-authored enclosure simulation (E014), not food packaging. The only keyword link to the challenge is the word 'mould' (mould tooling, not Botrytis mould). His project is semi-crystalline injection-moulding warpage (E177, E148) and his industry work is automotive plastics (E163); restrictions require partners to supply moulded parts and licences for proprietary simulation software (E176, E148). Nothing registered supports thermoformed rPET punnet/lidding-film or fruit-spoilage work, so lexical agreement on 'mould' is a false lead.
findings.recheckQuestion: Is there any registered Evidence that R0426 has worked on food packaging, thermoformed trays or microbial spoilage rather than injection-moulding warpage?

findings.explanation: R0715 (Bojan Grbić, ranked 2) is strong on heat-seal science — mLLDPE seal-initiation temperature, seal-layer formulation, peel vs burst acceptance, film ageing (E131/E102, E146, E047, E039, E027, E134, patent E045/E145) — but no registered Evidence addresses fruit, respiration-matched OTR, headspace gas composition or Botrytis. The evidence explicitly frames his work as VFFS film sealability (E150, E122) and the patent example is cited in the pool's own field pointers only via shared generic terms ('heat','seal','film','temperature'); the actual documents are about thermal sealing windows, not mould control. Additionally his notes state a preference for collaborations with access to production-scale extrusion equipment because his cast-film line cannot replicate industrial conditions (E110), and his open_to items are framed around seal-layer formulation with converters/resin suppliers (E008) — a partial mismatch with a converter that only needs film specification and punnets, not seal-layer R&D. His sealing contribution would be secondary at best and ranking him second overstates fit.
findings.recheckQuestion: Does any registered Evidence show R0715 applying seal or permeability expertise to fresh-produce spoilage outcomes?

findings.explanation: R0172 (Snežana Puzović, ranked 5) is the best-substantiated permeability/film-transport expert (OTR/WVTR vs temperature, E086, E168, E070, E135, E126, patent E024/E076). However her registered notes state she is available for new collaborations only from autumn 2026 onwards while finishing MONOBAR supervision commitments (E173), which conflicts with the challenge's roughly eight-month pre-next-season deadline and its need for trial work now. She also prefers that experimental work be conducted in her own laboratory (E173), while her open_to centres on barrier characterisation and measurement services rather than MAP specification for a berry exporter (E179, E128). Any plan relying on her for near-term simulated-transit trials must be checked against this start date.
findings.recheckQuestion: Can R0172 start before autumn 2026, and would she accept a scope centred on film-specification modelling rather than pure barrier characterisation?

findings.explanation: R0786 (Svetlana Sabo, ranked 6) is a hygrothermal-modelling and enclosure-physics specialist: condensation onset in polycarbonate/ABS housings, dew-point margins, cable-gland vapour ingress in electrical substation cabinets and thermostat/housing seal physics (E035, E118, E034, E049, E003, E083, E106). Her industry experience is outdoor metering cabinets and product certification disputes (E160), and her open_to is enclosure design for moisture control (E038). No registered Evidence involves packaged food, MAP, respiration-driven gas exchange or Botrytis. The shared terms 'sealed', 'condensation' and 'humidity' describe water-vapour behaviour in electronic housings with heat sources — a fundamentally different transport regime from micro-condensation inside a small sealed punnet driven by berry respiration. Treating her as a condensation expert for raspberry punnets would extrapolate beyond her evidence.
findings.recheckQuestion: Has R0786 ever worked on condensation inside food or produce packaging rather than electrical enclosures?

findings.explanation: R1044 (Branka Lalić, ranked 7) is scheduled for parental leave from October 2026 to approximately April 2027 (E004), which overlaps the deadline-critical window the challenge describes; only commitments starting before October 2026 can be accommodated. Her registered output is biopolymer/starch–protein reactive extrusion with property mapping including OTR (E117, E182, patent E125) and some co-authorship on seal-test work (E039, E134 via shared documents), but no registered Evidence covers fruit, Botrytis or produce MAP. Her open_to is biopolymer formulation/testing (E165) and the twin-screw line is limited to ~5 kg/h, constraining any punnet-scale prototyping (E004). Relevance to the stated film-grade/OTR-matching problem is peripheral.
findings.recheckQuestion: Would R1044's group add anything to rPET lidding-film specification within the eight-month window, and can work start before her October 2026 leave?

findings.explanation: R0084 (Petar Dobanovački, ranked 8) is a mechanical-testing/accelerated-ageing specialist for engineering and biomedical polymers: hygroscopic swelling of PEI parts, PA12 fatigue after humidity cycling, TPU catheter ageing (E099, E068, E137, E120). His only film-related link is being participant index 1 on the PERMTEMP permeability project (E017, E115), whose subject is a permeability reference dataset for polyolefin films (an instrument calibration/reference dataset rather than MAP design). Profile bio is empty and his industry experience is medical-device and compounding companies (E044); open_to is fatigue/ageing testing, climate chamber, CMM and medical-device certification consulting (E042). No registered Evidence supports Berry/Botrytis or produce-packaging work, so his rank-8 inclusion rests on shared words in a shared project.
findings.recheckQuestion: Does R0084 have any registered Evidence of produce-packaging or spoilage work beyond the shared PERMTEMP project participation?

findings.explanation: Reviewing the whole pool, the substantive raspberry/Botrytis/MAP content is concentrated almost entirely in R0976 (Jelena Marković): Serbian raspberry MAP gas-mix specifications with 14-day storage and Botrytis incidence (E138), pre-cooling and headspace equilibration effects on Botrytis (E073), OTR/CO₂TR film selection for small-format berry trays with finite-element gas-permeation modelling (E087), Botrytis predictive-model/digital-twin work (E040, E064), and MAP engineering design (E055). The remaining seven candidates' registered Evidence contains no berry-Botrytis outcome data, so a portfolio that treats several of them as equivalent berry-spoilage experts would rest on keyword proximity only. Note also that the pool is truncated (40 merged, 8 selected) with SEMANTIC_SUPPORT_UNASSESSED and NARROW_CHANNEL_COVERAGE; absence of contrary evidence for unselected researchers cannot be assumed. This is advisory, not a verdict on any final team, and does not constitute approval.

claims.text: Unresolved questions include whether the visible mould arises from field inoculum, pre-cooling delay, condensation, or atmosphere imbalance; how seal integrity and anti-fog film behaviour interact with micro-condensation on this rPET shell; and whether simulated transit will reproduce the real German/Netherlands destination outcomes.
limitations: These questions follow from source content as gaps, not from experimental data on FreshPak's product.

summary.text: Dr. Jelena Marković (R0976) is a strong partial match for C036-CH1: her attributed work covers raspberry MAP gas composition for Serbian export, film OTR/CO₂TR screening with permeation modelling, pre-cooling effects on Botrytis, and temperature-driven shelf-life prediction on real Serbian consignments. This addresses the modelling gap and the film-specification translation the company lacks, but it does not by itself guarantee <1% mould at day 14; a bounded trial is the appropriate next step.

technicalRationale.text: Raspberry-specific evidence: a 5% O₂/15% CO₂ atmosphere cut Botrytis incidence 63% versus air and held firmness for 12 days at 2 °C, giving a defensible starting point for atmosphere targets.

Film specification capability: 12-film OTR/CO₂TR screening with finite-element gas-permeation modelling shows a method to convert measured permeability and headspace data into a candidate specification, matching the company's stated need to translate OTR/CO₂TR numbers into a film grade.

Condensation and pre-cooling: evidence on forced-air versus room cooling and hydrocooling links equilibration speed and free moisture to Botrytis incidence, relevant to the company's micro-condensation hypothesis.

Cold-chain data use: existing work ingesting temperature/humidity streams into Botrytis-relevant prediction models indicates usable methodology for FreshPak's two seasons of logs and destination inspection reports.

cooperationScope.text: Scope: a film-specification and trial-design project using FreshPak's lab (OTR/CO₂TR, headspace gas, seal strength) and historic shipment data, with milestones (a) translation of logs into a temperature/humidity profile, (b) modelled headspace and Botrytis risk ranking for a short candidate film list, (c) simulated-transit trial protocol and its execution, (d) pre-season consignment check.
Engagement form to agree: joint project and/or industrial PhD co-supervision, consistent with the researcher's stated openness.

validation.text: Baseline: current lidding film and seal pressure run in the simulated-transit protocol, recording visible Botrytis incidence at days 9 and 14 and headspace O₂/CO₂. Candidate films are measured the same way, with model-predicted versus observed equilibrium gas composition compared per film and fill weight. Go/no-go: advance to the pre-season consignment check only if the best candidate reaches the agreed mould-incidence threshold and its observed headspace trend is consistent with the model; otherwise revise film, seal setting or pre-cooling before the season deadline.

constraints.text: Required inputs from FreshPak: the two current film grades and their measured OTR/CO₂TR, standard punnet geometry and fill weight, seal pressure range, two seasons of temperature/humidity logs and destination inspection reports, and lab time for headspace and seal testing. Engagement is limited to the researcher's lab and part-time involvement; no large external testing programme can be assumed given the stated budget.

What remains outside the supported scope: heat-seal and anti-fog film behaviour, micro-condensation control in the 125 g rPET shell, compostable-material migration, and full commercial deployment or a contractual one-percent mould guarantee.

unknowns.text: Open questions: which factor dominates visible mould (field inoculum, pre-cooling delay, condensation, atmosphere imbalance); how anti-fog chemistry and seal integrity interact with condensation; whether simulated transit reproduces German/Netherlands destination outcomes; and whether any candidate film can reach <1% at day 14 within budget.

findings.explanation: R0926 (Sofija Ristić, ranked 3) is a mechanical-engineering sealing-systems researcher whose registered corpus concerns elastomeric gaskets, O-rings and IP-rated electromechanical/enclosure housings: condensation inside sealed electrical enclosures (E014, E072), moisture ingress through compressed gaskets in IP54 steel cabinets (E012), FIP vs EPDM gaskets on electrical cabinets (E094). Her project MOISTMOD targets low-voltage electrical enclosure condensation modelling with a Python prediction tool (E007, E142). There is no registered Evidence of perishable-food, berry, MAP or food-packaging work, and her industry experience is enclosure/cabinet manufacturers (E127). Keyword overlap ('condensation', 'sealed', 'modelling') therefore does not establish technical suitability for Botrytis control in raspberry punnets; her 'modelling' expertise is heat-moisture transfer in non-food cavities, not respiration/permeability-based MAP design.
findings.recheckQuestion: Does R0926 have any registered Evidence of fresh-produce or food-packaging MAP work, as opposed to electromechanical enclosure condensation?

findings.explanation: R0426 (Aleksandar Bošković, ranked 4) contributes injection-moulding thermomechanical simulation: warpage/residual stress in PA6 and PP parts, mould heat-transfer-coefficient calibration and cooling-circuit CFD (E100, E172, E002, E108, E016, E111). His sole condensation-related item is a co-authored enclosure simulation (E014), not food packaging. The only keyword link to the challenge is the word 'mould' (mould tooling, not Botrytis mould). His project is semi-crystalline injection-moulding warpage (E177, E148) and his industry work is automotive plastics (E163); restrictions require partners to supply moulded parts and licences for proprietary simulation software (E176, E148). Nothing registered supports thermoformed rPET punnet/lidding-film or fruit-spoilage work, so lexical agreement on 'mould' is a false lead.
findings.recheckQuestion: Is there any registered Evidence that R0426 has worked on food packaging, thermoformed trays or microbial spoilage rather than injection-moulding warpage?

findings.explanation: R0715 (Bojan Grbić, ranked 2) is strong on heat-seal science — mLLDPE seal-initiation temperature, seal-layer formulation, peel vs burst acceptance, film ageing (E131/E102, E146, E047, E039, E027, E134, patent E045/E145) — but no registered Evidence addresses fruit, respiration-matched OTR, headspace gas composition or Botrytis. The evidence explicitly frames his work as VFFS film sealability (E150, E122) and the patent example is cited in the pool's own field pointers only via shared generic terms ('heat','seal','film','temperature'); the actual documents are about thermal sealing windows, not mould control. Additionally his notes state a preference for collaborations with access to production-scale extrusion equipment because his cast-film line cannot replicate industrial conditions (E110), and his open_to items are framed around seal-layer formulation with converters/resin suppliers (E008) — a partial mismatch with a converter that only needs film specification and punnets, not seal-layer R&D. His sealing contribution would be secondary at best and ranking him second overstates fit.
findings.recheckQuestion: Does any registered Evidence show R0715 applying seal or permeability expertise to fresh-produce spoilage outcomes?

findings.explanation: R0172 (Snežana Puzović, ranked 5) is the best-substantiated permeability/film-transport expert (OTR/WVTR vs temperature, E086, E168, E070, E135, E126, patent E024/E076). However her registered notes state she is available for new collaborations only from autumn 2026 onwards while finishing MONOBAR supervision commitments (E173), which conflicts with the challenge's roughly eight-month pre-next-season deadline and its need for trial work now. She also prefers that experimental work be conducted in her own laboratory (E173), while her open_to centres on barrier characterisation and measurement services rather than MAP specification for a berry exporter (E179, E128). Any plan relying on her for near-term simulated-transit trials must be checked against this start date.
findings.recheckQuestion: Can R0172 start before autumn 2026, and would she accept a scope centred on film-specification modelling rather than pure barrier characterisation?

findings.explanation: R0786 (Svetlana Sabo, ranked 6) is a hygrothermal-modelling and enclosure-physics specialist: condensation onset in polycarbonate/ABS housings, dew-point margins, cable-gland vapour ingress in electrical substation cabinets and thermostat/housing seal physics (E035, E118, E034, E049, E003, E083, E106). Her industry experience is outdoor metering cabinets and product certification disputes (E160), and her open_to is enclosure design for moisture control (E038). No registered Evidence involves packaged food, MAP, respiration-driven gas exchange or Botrytis. The shared terms 'sealed', 'condensation' and 'humidity' describe water-vapour behaviour in electronic housings with heat sources — a fundamentally different transport regime from micro-condensation inside a small sealed punnet driven by berry respiration. Treating her as a condensation expert for raspberry punnets would extrapolate beyond her evidence.
findings.recheckQuestion: Has R0786 ever worked on condensation inside food or produce packaging rather than electrical enclosures?

findings.explanation: R1044 (Branka Lalić, ranked 7) is scheduled for parental leave from October 2026 to approximately April 2027 (E004), which overlaps the deadline-critical window the challenge describes; only commitments starting before October 2026 can be accommodated. Her registered output is biopolymer/starch–protein reactive extrusion with property mapping including OTR (E117, E182, patent E125) and some co-authorship on seal-test work (E039, E134 via shared documents), but no registered Evidence covers fruit, Botrytis or produce MAP. Her open_to is biopolymer formulation/testing (E165) and the twin-screw line is limited to ~5 kg/h, constraining any punnet-scale prototyping (E004). Relevance to the stated film-grade/OTR-matching problem is peripheral.
findings.recheckQuestion: Would R1044's group add anything to rPET lidding-film specification within the eight-month window, and can work start before her October 2026 leave?

findings.explanation: R0084 (Petar Dobanovački, ranked 8) is a mechanical-testing/accelerated-ageing specialist for engineering and biomedical polymers: hygroscopic swelling of PEI parts, PA12 fatigue after humidity cycling, TPU catheter ageing (E099, E068, E137, E120). His only film-related link is being participant index 1 on the PERMTEMP permeability project (E017, E115), whose subject is a permeability reference dataset for polyolefin films (an instrument calibration/reference dataset rather than MAP design). Profile bio is empty and his industry experience is medical-device and compounding companies (E044); open_to is fatigue/ageing testing, climate chamber, CMM and medical-device certification consulting (E042). No registered Evidence supports Berry/Botrytis or produce-packaging work, so his rank-8 inclusion rests on shared words in a shared project.
findings.recheckQuestion: Does R0084 have any registered Evidence of produce-packaging or spoilage work beyond the shared PERMTEMP project participation?

findings.explanation: Reviewing the whole pool, the substantive raspberry/Botrytis/MAP content is concentrated almost entirely in R0976 (Jelena Marković): Serbian raspberry MAP gas-mix specifications with 14-day storage and Botrytis incidence (E138), pre-cooling and headspace equilibration effects on Botrytis (E073), OTR/CO₂TR film selection for small-format berry trays with finite-element gas-permeation modelling (E087), Botrytis predictive-model/digital-twin work (E040, E064), and MAP engineering design (E055). The remaining seven candidates' registered Evidence contains no berry-Botrytis outcome data, so a portfolio that treats several of them as equivalent berry-spoilage experts would rest on keyword proximity only. Note also that the pool is truncated (40 merged, 8 selected) with SEMANTIC_SUPPORT_UNASSESSED and NARROW_CHANNEL_COVERAGE; absence of contrary evidence for unselected researchers cannot be assumed. This is advisory, not a verdict on any final team, and does not constitute approval.
findings.recheckQuestion: If any candidate other than R0976 is presented as bringing berry-Botrytis outcome evidence, which registered Evidence ID supplies it?

findings.explanation: Only the eight fixed-pool candidates and their registered Evidence were inspected. No claim could be cited for the Proposer's (unseen) claims, so claimIds are empty throughout. Checks of the remaining 32 merged candidates, of whether any candidate's Evidence contains conflicting results, and of whether the challenge's sub-1% mould target is achievable by any candidate were not performed; the challenge text itself notes that two prior film-grade/seal-pressure trials did not reduce mould rates enough, which is a customer-stated constraint on expected effect size rather than candidate counter-evidence.
findings.recheckQuestion: Should the remaining merged candidates be inspected before any portfolio finalisation?

noCounterEvidenceFound: No blocking incompatibility was found between R0976's registered Evidence and the challenge's raspberry/Botrytis/MAP needs; no absent-attribution issue was found for any of the eight candidates (unattributedEvidenceIds empty, all content links backed by identity Evidence).
No explicit identity conflict (duplicate or contradictory researcher identity bindings) was found for any of the eight inspected candidates.

No counter-evidence was found indicating that the challenge's stated OTR/CO₂TR and headspace-measurement capability is incompatible with the pool's registered permeability instrumentation descriptions; this was not a proof of suitability, only that no contradiction appeared in inspected records.

findings.explanation: The draft's quantitative summaries match the original abstracts: E138 states the 5% O₂/15% CO₂ atmosphere reduced Botrytis incidence by 63% vs control, firmness above threshold 12 days vs 6 days, and marketability at day 10; C2 reports these figures and explicitly limits them ('relative to control, does not imply sub-1% absolute', 'sensory panel day 10 falls short of 14-day target'). E073 reports 38 vs 210 min cooling, 14 h earlier O₂ equilibration, lower Botrytis at day 8; C4 carries the same numbers and notes day-8 outcomes do not demonstrate day-14 performance. No overstated universal or deployment claim is present.
findings.recheckQuestion: Do the quoted numerical results in C2 and C4 remain identical to the values in E138 and E073?

findings.explanation: C3 attributes the 12-film OTR/CO₂TR screening, finite-element permeation modelling and 55% mould reduction to E087, and E140 confirms R0976 is author 3 on that record. The draft's limitation notes that the tray was mixed-berry and that the film spec (OTR 3,800, CO₂TR 18,000) cannot be transferred to the company's 125 g rPET punnet without local verification. The inference is therefore properly bounded; it does not claim the company's punnet will achieve the same result.
findings.recheckQuestion: Does C3 avoid asserting transferability of the mixed-berry film specification to the 125 g rPET punnet beyond local verification?

findings.explanation: C5's digital-twin figures (88% flagged, 9% false positives, four exporters, 240 consignments) match E040, and the Monte Carlo 91% coverage and 180 consignments match E064. E064 is on strawberry total aerobic count, and the draft says so in its limitation and notes that Botrytis-specific raspberry calibration is separate. This is honestly labelled and does not overstate the evidence as validated raspberry Botrytis prediction.
findings.recheckQuestion: Is the strawberry/aerobic-count basis of the Monte Carlo model disclosed and kept separate from Botrytis-specific prediction in the draft?

findings.explanation: E055 is a book chapter covering gas mass balance, film permeability selection, tray geometry effects on headspace equilibration and a worked forced-air pre-cooling + MAP example for a mid-sized raspberry exporter; C6 reproduces this and correctly frames it as a methodological reference, not validation. The technicalRationale line linked to C4 ('links equilibration speed and free moisture to Botrytis incidence, relevant to the company's micro-condensation hypothesis') stays within what E073 supports (hydrocooling free moisture promoting calyx decay) without claiming micro-condensation control is proven.
findings.recheckQuestion: Does the technicalRationale for C4 avoid claiming demonstrated micro-condensation control in the 125 g rPET punnet?

findings.explanation: The proposal sections correctly refuse to guarantee the customer's <1% day-14 target (C8, constraints, unknowns), describe a bounded film-specification/trial-design contribution grounded in the candidate's registered MAP/film/cold-chain work (C9, C10), and state the participation form as joint project and/or industrial PhD supervision consistent with E101/E015. C11's claim of prior work with three fruit exporters matches E015 verbatim, and the section correctly notes the exact engagement form is not specified. This meets the cooperation-support requirement with registered evidence of a concrete contribution to the core modelling gap, without implying unlimited availability, guaranteed success or completed deployment.
findings.recheckQuestion: Does the proposal continue to state the <1% day-14 outcome as the company's goal rather than a demonstrated result, and to confine the contribution to registered MAP/film/cold-chain competence?

Raspberries for Germany arrive with mould on day 9; buyers want 14 days.
We ship raspberries from Serbian packing houses to buyers in Germany and the Netherlands. The berries leave Serbia in good condition — our own quality checks confirm that — but by day nine of a typical fourteen-day shelf-life window, a meaningful share of punnets show visible Botrytis mould. Buyers have started issuing penalty deductions and two accounts have threatened to switch suppliers unless we fix this before next season, which means we have roughly eight months. The punnet itself is a standard 125 g rPET shell with a heat-sealed anti-fog lidding film. We have run informal trials with two different film grades and adjusted seal pressures, but mould rates did not drop enough to matter. We suspect the issue is a combination of micro-condensation inside the punnet and an oxygen-transmission rate that is not well matched to berry respiration at 2–4 °C. We have OTR and CO₂TR instruments in the lab and can measure headspace gas composition, but we do not have the modelling background to translate those numbers into a film specification. We also have real shipment data — temperature logs, humidity logs, and destination inspection reports — from the last two seasons. Budget for trials is limited; we can fund materials and lab time but cannot afford a large external testing programme. A good result is punnets reaching day fourteen with mould incidence below one percent, confirmed in controlled simulated-transit tests.

evidence.excerpt: Mixed-berry trays combining raspberry, blueberry, and blackberry are commercially attractive but present packaging engineering challenges because each species has a distinct optimal modified atmosphere range and a different respiration rate at equivalent temperatures. This study evaluated 12 commercially available polymeric packaging films differing in oxygen transmission rate (OTR) and carbon dioxide transmission rate (CO₂TR) for their suitability in MAP of mixed-berry trays stored at 2 °C. Headspace equilibrium gas compositions were measured at 24-hour intervals over eight days and compared against species-specific target ranges determined from prior single-species trials. Microbiological and firmness data were collected at four-day intervals. A film with OTR of 3,800 cm³/m²/day and CO₂TR of 18,000 cm³/m²/day delivered headspace conditions within acceptable ranges for all three species simultaneously and reduced mold incidence by 55% relative to a standard polyethylene control. Finite element modelling of gas permeation through the film was used to confirm experimental headspace trends and to predict equilibrium under alternative tray fill-weight scenarios. The results provide film specification guidance for packers handling mixed-berry formats and demonstrate that a single film solution can satisfy the conflicting atmosphere requirements of co-packaged fruit species.

Rapid and uniform pre-cooling of freshly harvested raspberries prior to MAP sealing is critical for establishing the target equilibrium atmosphere within packaging. This experimental study examined three pre-cooling protocols — forced-air cooling at 2 m/s, hydrocooling at 1 °C, and room cooling as control — applied to raspberry punnets subsequently sealed under a 5% O₂/15% CO₂ MAP at 2 °C storage. Headspace gas composition was monitored at 0, 6, 12, 24, and 48 hours post-sealing using an inline gas analyzer. Fruit core temperature profiles, firmness, respiration rate (CO₂ evolution), and drip loss were recorded throughout a 10-day storage trial. Forced-air cooling achieved target core temperature in 38 minutes compared to 210 minutes for room cooling, and resulted in target headspace O₂ equilibration 14 hours earlier than the room-cooled control. Faster equilibration was associated with significantly lower Botrytis incidence (p < 0.01) and superior firmness retention at day 8. Hydrocooling achieved comparable equilibration speed but introduced elevated free moisture that promoted calyx decay. The findings quantify the shelf-life benefit of investing in forced-air cooling infrastructure and inform revised pre-cooling standard operating procedures for export packers.

This study investigated the effect of modified atmosphere packaging (MAP) on the postharvest quality and shelf life of Serbian-grown raspberries intended for export markets. Three gas compositions — 5% O₂/15% CO₂/80% N₂, 10% O₂/10% CO₂/80% N₂, and ambient air control — were evaluated at 2 °C storage over a 14-day period. Quality parameters including firmness, color (L*, a*, b*), soluble solids content, titratable acidity, and visual mold incidence were monitored at two-day intervals. Microbiological analyses targeted total aerobic counts and Botrytis cinerea colony formation. Results demonstrated that the 5% O₂/15% CO₂ atmosphere reduced Botrytis incidence by 63% relative to control and maintained firmness above commercial acceptability thresholds for 12 days compared to 6 days in ambient conditions. Sensory panel scores for color and texture confirmed marketability at day 10 under optimal MAP conditions. The findings provide actionable gas-mix specifications for exporters shipping raspberries to Central European markets, and establish a data foundation for integrating MAP parameters into predictive shelf-life models. Practical recommendations for film permeability selection and pallet-level gas management are discussed.

Static best-before labelling does not reflect the actual quality state of perishable foods subjected to variable cold-chain conditions. A two-dimensional finite-volume model of moisture and heat transport was developed for a generic polycarbonate housing representative of handheld electronic devices. The domain included the polymer shell, an internal air cavity of 38 cm³, and a printed circuit board heat source. For a housing wall thickness of 2 mm with no desiccant, the dew-point margin dropped below zero during the cooling phase at hour 14, predicting condensation on the board. Raspberries for Germany arrive with mould on day 9; buyers want 14 days.
We ship raspberries from Serbian packing houses to buyers in Germany and the Netherlands. The berries leave Serbia in good condition — our own quality checks confirm that — but by day nine of a typical fourteen-day shelf-life window, a meaningful share of punnets show visible Botrytis mould. Buyers have started issuing penalty deductions and two accounts have threatened to switch suppliers unless we fix this before next season, which means we have roughly eight months. The punnet itself is a standard 125 g rPET shell with a heat-sealed anti-fog lidding film. We have run informal trials with two different film grades and adjusted seal pressures, but mould rates did not drop enough to matter. We suspect the issue is a combination of micro-condensation inside the punnet and an oxygen-transmission rate that is not well matched to berry respiration at 2–4 °C. We have OTR and CO₂TR instruments in the lab and can measure headspace gas composition, but we do not have the modelling background to translate those numbers into a film specification. We also have real shipment data — temperature logs, humidity logs, and destination inspection reports — from the last two seasons. Budget for trials is limited; we can fund materials and lab time but cannot afford a large external testing programme. A good result is punnets reaching day fourteen with mould incidence below one percent, confirmed in controlled simulated-transit tests.

findings.explanation: R0926 (Sofija Ristić, ranked 3) is a mechanical-engineering sealing-systems researcher whose registered corpus concerns elastomeric gaskets, O-rings and IP-rated electromechanical/enclosure housings: condensation inside sealed electrical enclosures (E014, E072), moisture ingress through compressed gaskets in IP54 steel cabinets (E012), FIP vs EPDM gaskets on electrical cabinets (E094). Her project MOISTMOD targets low-voltage electrical enclosure condensation modelling with a Python prediction tool (E007, E142). There is no registered Evidence of perishable-food, berry, MAP or food-packaging work, and her industry experience is enclosure/cabinet manufacturers (E127). Keyword overlap ('condensation', 'sealed', 'modelling') therefore does not establish technical suitability for Botrytis control in raspberry punnets; her 'modelling' expertise is heat-moisture transfer in non-food cavities, not respiration/permeability-based MAP design.
findings.recheckQuestion: Does R0926 have any registered Evidence of fresh-produce or food-packaging MAP work, as opposed to electromechanical enclosure condensation?

findings.explanation: R0426 (Aleksandar Bošković, ranked 4) contributes injection-moulding thermomechanical simulation: warpage/residual stress in PA6 and PP parts, mould heat-transfer-coefficient calibration and cooling-circuit CFD (E100, E172, E002, E108, E016, E111). His sole condensation-related item is a co-authored enclosure simulation (E014), not food packaging. The only keyword link to the challenge is the word 'mould' (mould tooling, not Botrytis mould). His project is semi-crystalline injection-moulding warpage (E177, E148) and his industry work is automotive plastics (E163); restrictions require partners to supply moulded parts and licences for proprietary simulation software (E176, E148). Nothing registered supports thermoformed rPET punnet/lidding-film or fruit-spoilage work, so lexical agreement on 'mould' is a false lead.
findings.recheckQuestion: Is there any registered Evidence that R0426 has worked on food packaging, thermoformed trays or microbial spoilage rather than injection-moulding warpage?

findings.explanation: R0715 (Bojan Grbić, ranked 2) is strong on heat-seal science — mLLDPE seal-initiation temperature, seal-layer formulation, peel vs burst acceptance, film ageing (E131/E102, E146, E047, E039, E027, E134, patent E045/E145) — but no registered Evidence addresses fruit, respiration-matched OTR, headspace gas composition or Botrytis. The evidence explicitly frames his work as VFFS film sealability (E150, E122) and the patent example is cited in the pool's own field pointers only via shared generic terms ('heat','seal','film','temperature'); the actual documents are about thermal sealing windows, not mould control. Additionally his notes state a preference for collaborations with access to production-scale extrusion equipment because his cast-film line cannot replicate industrial conditions (E110), and his open_to items are framed around seal-layer formulation with converters/resin suppliers (E008) — a partial mismatch with a converter that only needs film specification and punnets, not seal-layer R&D. His sealing contribution would be secondary at best and ranking him second overstates fit.
findings.recheckQuestion: Does any registered Evidence show R0715 applying seal or permeability expertise to fresh-produce spoilage outcomes?

findings.explanation: R0172 (Snežana Puzović, ranked 5) is the best-substantiated permeability/film-transport expert (OTR/WVTR vs temperature, E086, E168, E070, E135, E126, patent E024/E076). However her registered notes state she is available for new collaborations only from autumn 2026 onwards while finishing MONOBAR supervision commitments (E173), which conflicts with the challenge's roughly eight-month pre-next-season deadline and its need for trial work now. She also prefers that experimental work be conducted in her own laboratory (E173), while her open_to centres on barrier characterisation and measurement services rather than MAP specification for a berry exporter (E179, E128). Any plan relying on her for near-term simulated-transit trials must be checked against this start date.
findings.recheckQuestion: Can R0172 start before autumn 2026, and would she accept a scope centred on film-specification modelling rather than pure barrier characterisation?

findings.explanation: R0786 (Svetlana Sabo, ranked 6) is a hygrothermal-modelling and enclosure-physics specialist: condensation onset in polycarbonate/ABS housings, dew-point margins, cable-gland vapour ingress in electrical substation cabinets and thermostat/housing seal physics (E035, E118, E034, E049, E003, E083, E106). Her industry experience is outdoor metering cabinets and product certification disputes (E160), and her open_to is enclosure design for moisture control (E038). No registered Evidence involves packaged food, MAP, respiration-driven gas exchange or Botrytis. The shared terms 'sealed', 'condensation' and 'humidity' describe water-vapour behaviour in electronic housings with heat sources — a fundamentally different transport regime from micro-condensation inside a small sealed punnet driven by berry respiration. Treating her as a condensation expert for raspberry punnets would extrapolate beyond her evidence.
findings.recheckQuestion: Has R0786 ever worked on condensation inside food or produce packaging rather than electrical enclosures?

evidence.excerpt: Mixed-berry trays combining raspberry, blueberry, and blackberry are commercially attractive but present packaging engineering challenges because each species has a distinct optimal modified atmosphere range and a different respiration rate at equivalent temperatures. This study evaluated 12 commercially available polymeric packaging films differing in oxygen transmission rate (OTR) and carbon dioxide transmission rate (CO₂TR) for their suitability in MAP of mixed-berry trays stored at 2 °C. Headspace equilibrium gas compositions were measured at 24-hour intervals over eight days and compared against species-specific target ranges determined from prior single-species trials. Microbiological and firmness data were collected at four-day intervals. A film with OTR of 3,800 cm³/m²/day and CO₂TR of 18,000 cm³/m²/day delivered headspace conditions within acceptable ranges for all three species simultaneously and reduced mold incidence by 55% relative to a standard polyethylene control. Finite element modelling of gas permeation through the film was used to confirm experimental headspace trends and to predict equilibrium under alternative tray fill-weight scenarios. The results provide film specification guidance for packers handling mixed-berry formats and demonstrate that a single film solution can satisfy the conflicting atmosphere requirements of co-packaged fruit species.

Rapid and uniform pre-cooling of freshly harvested raspberries prior to MAP sealing is critical for establishing the target equilibrium atmosphere within packaging. This experimental study examined three pre-cooling protocols — forced-air cooling at 2 m/s, hydrocooling at 1 °C, and room cooling as control — applied to raspberry punnets subsequently sealed under a 5% O₂/15% CO₂ MAP at 2 °C storage. Headspace gas composition was monitored at 0, 6, 12, 24, and 48 hours post-sealing using an inline gas analyzer. Fruit core temperature profiles, firmness, respiration rate (CO₂ evolution), and drip loss were recorded throughout a 10-day storage trial. Forced-air cooling achieved target core temperature in 38 minutes compared to 210 minutes for room cooling, and resulted in target headspace O₂ equilibration 14 hours earlier than the room-cooled control. Faster equilibration was associated with significantly lower Botrytis incidence (p < 0.01) and superior firmness retention at day 8. Hydrocooling achieved comparable equilibration speed but introduced elevated free moisture that promoted calyx decay. The findings quantify the shelf-life benefit of investing in forced-air cooling infrastructure and inform revised pre-cooling standard operating procedures for export packers.

This study investigated the effect of modified atmosphere packaging (MAP) on the postharvest quality and shelf life of Serbian-grown raspberries intended for export markets. Three gas compositions — 5% O₂/15% CO₂/80% N₂, 10% O₂/10% CO₂/80% N₂, and ambient air control — were evaluated at 2 °C storage over a 14-day period. Quality parameters including firmness, color (L*, a*, b*), soluble solids content, titratable acidity, and visual mold incidence were monitored at two-day intervals. Microbiological analyses targeted total aerobic counts and Botrytis cinerea colony formation. Results demonstrated that the 5% O₂/15% CO₂ atmosphere reduced Botrytis incidence by 63% relative to control and maintained firmness above commercial acceptability thresholds for 12 days compared to 6 days in ambient conditions. Sensory panel scores for color and texture confirmed marketability at day 10 under optimal MAP conditions. The findings provide actionable gas-mix specifications for exporters shipping raspberries to Central European markets, and establish a data foundation for integrating MAP parameters into predictive shelf-life models. Practical recommendations for film permeability selection and pallet-level gas management are discussed.

Static best-before labelling does not reflect the actual quality state of perishable foods subjected to variable cold-chain conditions. This paper reports a feasibility study for implementing sensor-based dynamic remaining shelf-life (RSL) labelling on raspberry and blueberry consignments exported from Serbia. Time-temperature indicator (TTI) labels from two commercial suppliers were benchmarked against data-logger-calibrated predictive model outputs for Botrytis growth and total aerobic count across 24 simulated and 16 real export consignments. TTI colour-response kinetics were characterised at 0, 4, 8, and 12 °C and integrated into an RSL calculation algorithm using an Arrhenius-based temperature dependence model. Agreement between TTI-derived RSL and model-derived RSL was within ±1.2 days for 79% of consignments, which was deemed commercially acceptable by participating exporters. A cost–benefit analysis estimated that TTI-based RSL labelling could reduce consignment rejection rates at destination by 18–24%, yielding a positive return on investment for exporters operating above 50 tonnes per season. Regulatory and labelling compliance considerations under EU food law are discussed, along with the data requirements for formal TTI validation. The study supports the case for piloting RSL labelling in the Serbian berry export sector as part of a broader cold-chain quality assurance programme.

Active packaging systems incorporating volatile antimicrobial agents derived from plant extracts represent a promising complement to conventional modified atmosphere packaging (MAP) for fresh blueberries. This study assessed the efficacy of sachets containing encapsulated thymol and carvacrol — sourced from wild thyme and oregano — integrated into clamshell packaging under a 5% O₂/15% CO₂ atmosphere at 2 °C. Blueberry quality was monitored over 18 days for firmness, total anthocyanin content, weight loss, and microbiological load (total aerobic count and Botrytis incidence). Active MAP sachets reduced total aerobic counts by 1.8 log CFU/g relative to passive MAP controls at day 12 and delayed visible mold onset by four days. Anthocyanin retention was significantly higher in active MAP treatments (p < 0.05), suggesting a secondary antioxidant protective effect. Consumer acceptability scores obtained through a 40-member sensory panel confirmed marketable quality at day 14 for saline-active MAP versus day 10 for passive MAP controls. Migration testing confirmed that thymol and carvacrol residues in fruit tissue remained below European regulatory thresholds. This work demonstrates the practical feasibility of combining MAP gas composition with natural antimicrobial active elements for export-grade blueberry packaging.

Digital twin frameworks — virtual replicas of physical supply chains updated by real-time sensor data — offer a new paradigm for proactive spoilage management in perishable food logistics. This paper describes the integration of validated predictive microbial growth models for Botrytis cinerea and total aerobic bacteria into a digital twin architecture developed for Serbian berry cold-chain operations. The system ingests temperature and relative humidity streams from IoT sensors placed within refrigerated transport units and storage rooms, feeding real-time inputs into a model library calibrated for raspberry, blueberry, and strawberry substrates. A graphical dashboard presents logistics managers with dynamically updated remaining shelf-life estimates and spoilage risk scores for each consignment. A 12-month pilot deployment covering four exporting companies and 240 consignments demonstrated that digital twin alerts correctly flagged 88% of consignments subsequently confirmed to exhibit elevated spoilage at destination. False-positive rates were 9%, attributed primarily to anomalous sensor placement near evaporator coils. Integration with enterprise resource planning (ERP) systems for automated re-routing decisions is discussed as a near-term development pathway. The study establishes a reproducible blueprint for deploying predictive microbiology within commercial cold-chain digital twin platforms in the Serbian fruit export sector.

Deterministic predictive models assume fixed temperature inputs, which rarely reflect the stochastic nature of real-world cold-chain environments. This study presents a stochastic modelling framework for predicting the remaining shelf life of fresh strawberries under realistic fluctuating temperature conditions. A Monte Carlo simulation approach was applied to propagate uncertainty in temperature distribution parameters — derived from 180 sensor-monitored consignments — through a validated secondary model for total aerobic count growth on strawberry. Output distributions of predicted shelf life were compared against observed microbiological end-point data from the same consignments. The stochastic model significantly outperformed its deterministic equivalent in capturing the spread of observed outcomes, with prediction intervals covering 91% of empirical data points. Sensitivity analysis identified mean transport temperature and frequency of door-opening events as the two variables contributing most to shelf-life variance. A simplified probabilistic shelf-life index (PSI) was derived for use by quality managers without specialist modelling expertise. The framework is applicable to other soft fruits and other pathogen or spoilage organism combinations, provided primary growth data are available. This work advances the practical deployment of quantitative risk-informed decision-making in Serbian berry export supply chains.

This book chapter provides a comprehensive treatment of the engineering principles underpinning postharvest preservation of fresh horticultural products, with emphasis on modified atmosphere packaging and cold-chain management. The chapter opens with a review of the biochemical and microbiological deterioration mechanisms that govern shelf life in soft fruits, including ethylene-mediated ripening, oxidative browning, and fungal pathogen proliferation. It then develops the engineering framework for MAP system design, covering gas mass balance modelling, film permeability selection, and tray geometry effects on headspace equilibration dynamics. Cold-chain management is addressed through the lens of predictive microbiology, explaining how primary and secondary models can be linked to temperature monitoring data to generate real-time shelf-life estimates. A section on supply chain integration discusses how MAP and predictive modelling tools can be embedded in digital logistics systems. Case studies drawn from Serbian berry export operations illustrate the translation of laboratory models into operational practice, including a worked example of a forced-air pre-cooling and MAP line for a mid-sized raspberry exporter. The chapter concludes with a forward-looking discussion of emerging active packaging technologies and AI-assisted cold-chain optimisation. It is intended for graduate students and food industry engineers seeking a practically oriented reference.

The effect of oven ageing at 80 °C for periods of 0, 7, 14, 21 and 28 days on the properties of two mLLDPE cast films was investigated to assess fitness for shelf-life-extended food packaging. Films were evaluated by DSC (crystallinity, melting peak), tensile testing (yield stress, elongation at break), and seal strength at a fixed jaw temperature of 115 °C. After 28 days, crystallinity increased by 3.1–4.7 percentage points in both grades, consistent with post-crystallisation. Yield stress rose by 8–12 %, while elongation at break declined from 620 % to 490–530 %, indicating embrittlement. Seal strength dropped by 12–17 % relative to the unaged films, attributed to increased crystallinity at the film surface reducing interdiffusion during sealing. Oxidation induction time measured by DSC-OIT at 200 °C under oxygen remained above 25 min for both grades after 28 days, indicating that the primary antioxidant package was not depleted. The results suggest a conservative shelf life of 18 months for sealed rolls stored below 35 °C.

A two-dimensional transient finite-element model of heat transfer from flat seal jaws through a multilayer OPP/tie/mLLDPE film stack was developed and validated against thermocouple measurements embedded in films at 0.1 s time resolution. Film layer thermal conductivities were taken from the literature (mLLDPE: 0.35 W/m·K; OPP: 0.22 W/m·K); jaw face temperature was set to experimentally measured values between 110 and 135 °C. Model predictions of seal-interface temperature matched experimental values with a mean absolute error of 1.8 °C across 48 test conditions. Simulations were then used to assess how jaw pressure (0.1–0.5 N/mm²) and dwell time (0.2–0.8 s) influence the time spent above the seal-initiation temperature of 97 °C at the film interface. Results show that for jaw temperatures at or below 115 °C, reducing dwell time below 0.35 s prevents the interface from reaching SIT even at maximum jaw pressure. The model provides a practical tool for setting sealing parameters without exhaustive trial runs.

This paper reports a formulation development exercise carried out with a regional flexible-packaging converter. The target was to lower the required jaw temperature on a 300 bags/min VFFS line from 125 °C to below 110 °C without reducing seal strength below 25 N/25 mm or compromising hot-tack performance. Starting from a commercial 40 µm mLLDPE monolayer film, two modifications were evaluated: (i) partial substitution of the mLLDPE base resin with a 1-octene-based very-low-density polyethylene (VLDPE, density 0.900 g/cm³) at 10–25 wt%, and (ii) increasing seal-layer thickness from 40 to 50 µm in a three-layer coextrudate with OPP and tie. VLDPE addition at 20 wt% lowered SIT by 9 °C and enabled 26 N/25 mm plateau seal strength at 108 °C. Increasing film thickness to 50 µm without VLDPE gave a 5 °C SIT reduction. The combination of 20 wt% VLDPE and 50 µm gauge achieved a usable sealing window of 106–138 °C, a 32 °C range versus 18 °C for the commercial film. Line trials on a production VFFS machine confirmed seal integrity of filled pouches under 1.5 bar air pressure.

The project investigated the relationship between seal-layer formulation variables—resin type, comonomer content, blend ratios, and film thickness—and the achievable thermal processing window on VFFS packaging lines running at up to 300 bags/min. Work was conducted across four tasks: rheological and thermal characterisation of candidate resins; cast-film extrusion trials on the laboratory line at the Faculty of Technology; heat-seal testing using a gradient sealer and a laboratory VFFS unit; and statistical modelling of composition–property relationships using RSM. The project produced seven publications and validated two target formulations with an industrial partner. A trained PhD student and two master's students were involved. Equipment procured under the project included an updated hot-tack tester and an ATR-FTIR accessory.

Two standard seal-quality tests—the 180° peel test and the differential pressure burst test—were applied to heat-sealed pouches made from OPP/tie/mLLDPE films sealed across a jaw temperature range of 95–140 °C. For each jaw temperature, 20 pouches were prepared and tested by both methods. Peel force data and burst pressure data were analysed for correlation and for their ability to discriminate between adequate and inadequate seals. The two methods agreed in classifying seals above 110 °C as acceptable (peel ≥ 25 N/25 mm; burst ≥ 180 kPa), but diverged in the 100–109 °C zone, where 7 of 20 pouches passed the burst test but failed the peel criterion. Root-cause analysis by SEM cross-section showed incomplete interdiffusion at the seal interface in those pouches. Repeatability expressed as coefficient of variation was 5.8 % for peel and 9.2 % for burst across all jaw temperatures. The peel test is recommended as the more conservative acceptance criterion for VFFS applications handling liquid or particulate products.

A blend composition for the seal layer of cast polyolefin films comprising 65–80 wt% metallocene linear low-density polyethylene with 1-octene comonomer, 15–25 wt% very-low-density polyethylene with density in the range 0.895–0.905 g/cm³, and 5–10 wt% low-density polyethylene with melt flow index below 1.0 g/10 min. The composition achieves a seal-initiation temperature below 100 °C at standard jaw conditions (0.3 N/mm², 0.4 s) and a plateau seal strength above 27 N/25 mm, providing a usable sealing window of at least 30 °C. Applicable to monolayer films and as the seal layer of coextruded or laminated multilayer structures for VFFS packaging.

Three-layer films with an oriented polypropylene (OPP) structural layer, an adhesive tie layer, and an mLLDPE seal layer were produced by lamination. Seal-layer thickness was varied at 10, 15, 20, 25 and 30 µm while total film gauge was held at 60 µm. Sealing experiments were conducted on a laboratory gradient heat-sealer over a 85–140 °C jaw temperature range; dwell time was fixed at 0.4 s and jaw pressure at 0.25 N/mm². Seal strength and hot-tack force were measured. Films with 20 µm seal layers achieved plateau seal strength of 31 N/25 mm and maintained hot-tack force above 6 N/25 mm over a 28 °C window (108–136 °C). Reducing the seal layer to 10 µm narrowed the hot-tack window to 16 °C and lowered plateau seal strength to 22 N/25 mm; increasing to 30 µm provided no significant benefit. Optical microscopy of cross-sections confirmed nominal thicknesses within ±1.5 µm. The 20 µm seal layer is proposed as the practical optimum for this film construction.

Seal-initiation temperature (SIT) is a primary determinant of packaging line throughput on vertical form–fill–seal machines. This work compared cast films produced from four mLLDPE resins differing in comonomer type (1-butene, 1-hexene, or 1-octene) at constant density (0.918 g/cm³) and melt flow index (2.0 g/10 min). Films of 40 µm nominal thickness were extruded on a laboratory cast-film line and sealed over a 90–135 °C range at 0.3 N/mm² and 0.5 s dwell time. Seal strength was measured by 180° peel on a tensile tester. The 1-octene grade yielded the lowest SIT (97 °C) and a plateau seal strength of 28 N/25 mm, compared to 108 °C and 22 N/25 mm for the 1-butene grade. DSC melting profiles correlated well with the observed SIT differences. Hot-tack measurements at 500 mm/s jaw separation confirmed that 1-octene resins provide a 14 °C wider hot-tack window, relevant for high-speed filling lines.

A cross-border collaboration between the Faculty of Technology Novi Sad and the Department of Plastics Technology at Budapest University of Technology, co-funded under Interreg IPA. The project addressed gaps in the regional packaging film industry by developing shared test protocols for heat-seal quality assessment and transferring extensional rheology measurement competence to the Serbian side. Grbić led Work Package 2, covering heat-seal and hot-tack testing protocol harmonisation and the comparative study of 180° peel versus burst test methods. Joint workshops were held in both Novi Sad and Budapest. A shared database of polymer melt rheology and seal-performance data was compiled and made available to packaging SMEs in both countries.

Grbić has expressed a preference for collaborations that can access production-scale extrusion equipment, as the laboratory cast-film line is limited to 45 mm screw diameter and cannot replicate all industrial conditions. He is not currently on sabbatical and is available for new project discussions.

A two-dimensional finite-difference model was developed to simulate transient heat and moisture transfer in a sealed steel enclosure containing a heat-dissipating printed circuit board. The model couples Fourier conduction through the walls with Fickian vapour diffusion and accounts for condensation on internal surfaces when local temperature drops below the dew point. Internal heat generation was set at 5 W, representing a typical low-power controller unit. Simulations were run for a 24-hour diurnal ambient profile representative of a Pannonian autumn day. Results showed that condensation first occurred on the lower half of the front panel after approximately 17 minutes of rapid external temperature drop at −1.2 °C/min. Increasing the initial internal air volume by 30 % by deepening the enclosure reduced condensation onset time by only 4 minutes, while adding a 2-g silica-gel desiccant delayed onset by 38 minutes. The model was validated against thermocouple and humidity logger measurements from a physical enclosure subjected to a controlled temperature ramp in a climate chamber.

Modelling Moisture Transport and Condensation Risk in Sealed Enclosures for Low-Voltage Infrastructure

Four commercial IP54-rated steel enclosures were instrumented with capacitive humidity sensors inside and outside, and temperature sensors at the wall mid-plane and external surface. They were mounted on a south-facing outdoor test rack in Novi Sad from March to October 2013. Internal relative humidity tracked external daily temperature cycles with a phase lag of approximately 3–4 hours. Total cumulative moisture ingress over the measurement period ranged from 4.2 to 7.8 g per enclosure, varying with seal type and mounting orientation. A one-dimensional transient diffusion model driven by measured vapour-pressure gradients reproduced the seasonal trend with a mean absolute error below 12 % when an effective diffusivity of 3.1 × 10⁻¹² m²/s was used for the compressed gasket region. The model indicates that horizontal lid orientation with a downward-facing seal gap reduces ingress by approximately 35 % compared with vertical orientation.

Foam-in-place (FIP) polyurethane gaskets applied to twelve sheet-metal electrical cabinet covers were compared with die-cut EPDM strips on twelve matched cabinets over a 36-month outdoor exposure period in a semi-urban environment near Novi Sad. Both cabinet populations were inspected every six months for visual defects, and sample gaskets were removed annually for laboratory compression-set and Shore A testing. FIP gaskets maintained lower compression-set values (mean 17 % at 36 months) compared with EPDM strips (mean 29 %), and showed less dimensional variability across the bead cross-section. However, four FIP samples exhibited adhesion loss at corners after 24 months when substrate surface preparation was below the specified cleanliness grade. Internal humidity loggers showed that cabinets with FIP gaskets experienced 11 % fewer condensation events over the monitoring period. Cost-benefit analysis incorporating material, application labour, and seal replacement is also presented.

Fourteen silicone O-rings were removed from photovoltaic string combiner boxes that had been in service for approximately five years at three sites across Vojvodina. Three accelerated ageing protocols for thermoplastic polyurethane (TPU) catheter tubing segments are compared: elevated temperature immersion (70 °C in phosphate-buffered saline), combined UV/humidity exposure (UVA, 0.76 W/m², 50% RH), and real-time ageing at 23 °C/50% RH over 52 weeks. Fatigue life under cyclic bending (displacement-controlled, 1 Hz, 180° bend radius) was measured for each protocol at nominal ageing equivalents of 6, 12, 24, and 52 weeks. The elevated temperature protocol was the most aggressive: fatigue life after 24-week equivalent ageing dropped to 42% of the initial value. Molecular weight (GPC), hardness (Shore A), and elongation at break were measured alongside fatigue data. Arrhenius correlation between the 70 °C and 23 °C datasets yielded an activation energy of 84 kJ/mol, within the range expected for hydrolytic degradation of polyester-based TPU. The UV/humidity protocol produced divergent results not predictable from the thermal model, suggesting a different degradation mechanism relevant only to external device surfaces.

This paper investigates whether DMA measurements—specifically storage modulus E′, loss modulus E″, and the loss tangent tan δ recorded at 1, 10, and 100 Hz—can serve as rapid non-destructive predictors of residual fatigue life in humidity-aged polymer specimens without performing full fatigue tests. POM-C and PEEK showed weaker correlations (r = −0.61 and −0.54), consistent with their low moisture uptake limiting the DMA-detectable change. A simple regression-based screening criterion using tan δ thresholds is proposed and its applicability limits are discussed.

sources.value: Mixed-berry trays combining raspberry, blueberry, and blackberry are commercially attractive but present packaging engineering challenges because each species has a distinct optimal modified atmosphere range and a different respiration rate at equivalent temperatures. This study evaluated 12 commercially available polymeric packaging films differing in oxygen transmission rate (OTR) and carbon dioxide transmission rate (CO₂TR) for their suitability in MAP of mixed-berry trays stored at 2 °C. Headspace equilibrium gas compositions were measured at 24-hour intervals over eight days and compared against species-specific target ranges determined from prior single-species trials. Microbiological and firmness data were collected at four-day intervals. A film with OTR of 3,800 cm³/m²/day and CO₂TR of 18,000 cm³/m²/day delivered headspace conditions within acceptable ranges for all three species simultaneously and reduced mold incidence by 55% relative to a standard polyethylene control. Finite element modelling of gas permeation through the film was used to confirm experimental headspace trends and to predict equilibrium under alternative tray fill-weight scenarios. The results provide film specification guidance for packers handling mixed-berry formats and demonstrate that a single film solution can satisfy the conflicting atmosphere requirements of co-packaged fruit species.

sources.value: Rapid and uniform pre-cooling of freshly harvested raspberries prior to MAP sealing is critical for establishing the target equilibrium atmosphere within packaging. This experimental study examined three pre-cooling protocols — forced-air cooling at 2 m/s, hydrocooling at 1 °C, and room cooling as control — applied to raspberry punnets subsequently sealed under a 5% O₂/15% CO₂ MAP at 2 °C storage. Headspace gas composition was monitored at 0, 6, 12, 24, and 48 hours post-sealing using an inline gas analyzer. Fruit core temperature profiles, firmness, respiration rate (CO₂ evolution), and drip loss were recorded throughout a 10-day storage trial. Forced-air cooling achieved target core temperature in 38 minutes compared to 210 minutes for room cooling, and resulted in target headspace O₂ equilibration 14 hours earlier than the room-cooled control. Faster equilibration was associated with significantly lower Botrytis incidence (p < 0.01) and superior firmness retention at day 8. Hydrocooling achieved comparable equilibration speed but introduced elevated free moisture that promoted calyx decay. The findings quantify the shelf-life benefit of investing in forced-air cooling infrastructure and inform revised pre-cooling standard operating procedures for export packers.

sources.value: This study investigated the effect of modified atmosphere packaging (MAP) on the postharvest quality and shelf life of Serbian-grown raspberries intended for export markets. Three gas compositions — 5% O₂/15% CO₂/80% N₂, 10% O₂/10% CO₂/80% N₂, and ambient air control — were evaluated at 2 °C storage over a 14-day period. Quality parameters including firmness, color (L*, a*, b*), soluble solids content, titratable acidity, and visual mold incidence were monitored at two-day intervals. Microbiological analyses targeted total aerobic counts and Botrytis cinerea colony formation. Results demonstrated that the 5% O₂/15% CO₂ atmosphere reduced Botrytis incidence by 63% relative to control and maintained firmness above commercial acceptability thresholds for 12 days compared to 6 days in ambient conditions. Sensory panel scores for color and texture confirmed marketability at day 10 under optimal MAP conditions. The findings provide actionable gas-mix specifications for exporters shipping raspberries to Central European markets, and establish a data foundation for integrating MAP parameters into predictive shelf-life models. Practical recommendations for film permeability selection and pallet-level gas management are discussed.

sources.value: Static best-before labelling does not reflect the actual quality state of perishable foods subjected to variable cold-chain conditions. This paper reports a feasibility study for implementing sensor-based dynamic remaining shelf-life (RSL) labelling on raspberry and blueberry consignments exported from Serbia. Time-temperature indicator (TTI) labels from two commercial suppliers were benchmarked against data-logger-calibrated predictive model outputs for Botrytis growth and total aerobic count across 24 simulated and 16 real export consignments. TTI colour-response kinetics were characterised at 0, 4, 8, and 12 °C and integrated into an RSL calculation algorithm using an Arrhenius-based temperature dependence model. Agreement between TTI-derived RSL and model-derived RSL was within ±1.2 days for 79% of consignments, which was deemed commercially acceptable by participating exporters. A cost–benefit analysis estimated that TTI-based RSL labelling could reduce consignment rejection rates at destination by 18–24%, yielding a positive return on investment for exporters operating above 50 tonnes per season. Regulatory and labelling compliance considerations under EU food law are discussed, along with the data requirements for formal TTI validation. The study supports the case for piloting RSL labelling in the Serbian berry export sector as part of a broader cold-chain quality assurance programme.

sources.value: Active packaging systems incorporating volatile antimicrobial agents derived from plant extracts represent a promising complement to conventional modified atmosphere packaging (MAP) for fresh blueberries. This study assessed the efficacy of sachets containing encapsulated thymol and carvacrol — sourced from wild thyme and oregano — integrated into clamshell packaging under a 5% O₂/15% CO₂ atmosphere at 2 °C. Blueberry quality was monitored over 18 days for firmness, total anthocyanin content, weight loss, and microbiological load (total aerobic count and Botrytis incidence). Active MAP sachets reduced total aerobic counts by 1.8 log CFU/g relative to passive MAP controls at day 12 and delayed visible mold onset by four days. Anthocyanin retention was significantly higher in active MAP treatments (p < 0.05), suggesting a secondary antioxidant protective effect. Consumer acceptability scores obtained through a 40-member sensory panel confirmed marketable quality at day 14 for saline-active MAP versus day 10 for passive MAP controls. Migration testing confirmed that thymol and carvacrol residues in fruit tissue remained below European regulatory thresholds. This work demonstrates the practical feasibility of combining MAP gas composition with natural antimicrobial active elements for export-grade blueberry packaging.

Digital twin frameworks — virtual replicas of physical supply chains updated by real-time sensor data — offer a new paradigm for proactive spoilage management in perishable food logistics. This paper describes the integration of validated predictive microbial growth models for Botrytis cinerea and total aerobic bacteria into a digital twin architecture developed for Serbian berry cold-chain operations. The system ingests temperature and relative humidity streams from IoT sensors placed within refrigerated transport units and storage rooms, feeding real-time inputs into a model library calibrated for raspberry, blueberry, and strawberry substrates. A graphical dashboard presents logistics managers with dynamically updated remaining shelf-life estimates and spoilage risk scores for each consignment. A 12-month pilot deployment covering four exporting companies and 240 consignments demonstrated that digital twin alerts correctly flagged 88% of consignments subsequently confirmed to exhibit elevated spoilage at destination. False-positive rates were 9%, attributed primarily to anomalous sensor placement near evaporator coils. Integration with enterprise resource planning (ERP) systems for automated re-routing decisions is discussed as a near-term development pathway. The study establishes a reproducible blueprint for deploying predictive microbiology within commercial cold-chain digital twin platforms in the Serbian fruit export sector.

sources.value: Deterministic predictive models assume fixed temperature inputs, which rarely reflect the stochastic nature of real-world cold-chain environments. This study presents a stochastic modelling framework for predicting the remaining shelf life of fresh strawberries under realistic fluctuating temperature conditions. A Monte Carlo simulation approach was applied to propagate uncertainty in temperature distribution parameters — derived from 180 sensor-monitored consignments — through a validated secondary model for total aerobic count growth on strawberry. Output distributions of predicted shelf life were compared against observed microbiological end-point data from the same consignments. The stochastic model significantly outperformed its deterministic equivalent in capturing the spread of observed outcomes, with prediction intervals covering 91% of empirical data points. Sensitivity analysis identified mean transport temperature and frequency of door-opening events as the two variables contributing most to shelf-life variance. A simplified probabilistic shelf-life index (PSI) was derived for use by quality managers without specialist modelling expertise. The framework is applicable to other soft fruits and other pathogen or spoilage organism combinations, provided primary growth data are available. This work advances the practical deployment of quantitative risk-informed decision-making in Serbian berry export supply chains.

sources.value: This book chapter provides a comprehensive treatment of the engineering principles underpinning postharvest preservation of fresh horticultural products, with emphasis on modified atmosphere packaging and cold-chain management. The chapter opens with a review of the biochemical and microbiological deterioration mechanisms that govern shelf life in soft fruits, including ethylene-mediated ripening, oxidative browning, and fungal pathogen proliferation. It then develops the engineering framework for MAP system design, covering gas mass balance modelling, film permeability selection, and tray geometry effects on headspace equilibration dynamics. Cold-chain management is addressed through the lens of predictive microbiology, explaining how primary and secondary models can be linked to temperature monitoring data to generate real-time shelf-life estimates. A section on supply chain integration discusses how MAP and predictive modelling tools can be embedded in digital logistics systems. Case studies drawn from Serbian berry export operations illustrate the translation of laboratory models into operational practice, including a worked example of a forced-air pre-cooling and MAP line for a mid-sized raspberry exporter. The chapter concludes with a forward-looking discussion of emerging active packaging technologies and AI-assisted cold-chain optimisation. It is intended for graduate students and food industry engineers seeking a practically oriented reference.

The effect of oven ageing at 80 °C for periods of 0, 7, 14, 21 and 28 days on the properties of two mLLDPE cast films was investigated to assess fitness for shelf-life-extended food packaging. Films were evaluated by DSC (crystallinity, melting peak), tensile testing (yield stress, elongation at break), and seal strength at a fixed jaw temperature of 115 °C. After 28 days, crystallinity increased by 3.1–4.7 percentage points in both grades, consistent with post-crystallisation. Yield stress rose by 8–12 %, while elongation at break declined from 620 % to 490–530 %, indicating embrittlement. Seal strength dropped by 12–17 % relative to the unaged films, attributed to increased crystallinity at the film surface reducing interdiffusion during sealing. Oxidation induction time measured by DSC-OIT at 200 °C under oxygen remained above 25 min for both grades after 28 days, indicating that the primary antioxidant package was not depleted. The results suggest a conservative shelf life of 18 months for sealed rolls stored below 35 °C.
