sources.value: A two-dimensional transient finite-element model of heat transfer from flat seal jaws through a multilayer OPP/tie/mLLDPE film stack was developed and validated against thermocouple measurements embedded in films at 0.1 s time resolution. Film layer thermal conductivities were taken from the literature (mLLDPE: 0.35 W/m·K; OPP: 0.22 W/m·K); jaw face temperature was set to experimentally measured values between 110 and 135 °C. Model predictions of seal-interface temperature matched experimental values with a mean absolute error of 1.8 °C across 48 test conditions. Simulations were then used to assess how jaw pressure (0.1–0.5 N/mm²) and dwell time (0.2–0.8 s) influence the time spent above the seal-initiation temperature of 97 °C at the film interface. Results show that for jaw temperatures at or below 115 °C, reducing dwell time below 0.35 s prevents the interface from reaching SIT even at maximum jaw pressure. The model provides a practical tool for setting sealing parameters without exhaustive trial runs.

This paper reports a formulation development exercise carried out with a regional flexible-packaging converter. The target was to lower the required jaw temperature on a 300 bags/min VFFS line from 125 °C to below 110 °C without reducing seal strength below 25 N/25 mm or compromising hot-tack performance. Starting from a commercial 40 µm mLLDPE monolayer film, two modifications were evaluated: (i) partial substitution of the mLLDPE base resin with a 1-octene-based very-low-density polyethylene (VLDPE, density 0.900 g/cm³) at 10–25 wt%, and (ii) increasing seal-layer thickness from 40 to 50 µm in a three-layer coextrudate with OPP and tie. VLDPE addition at 20 wt% lowered SIT by 9 °C and enabled 26 N/25 mm plateau seal strength at 108 °C. Increasing film thickness to 50 µm without VLDPE gave a 5 °C SIT reduction. The combination of 20 wt% VLDPE and 50 µm gauge achieved a usable sealing window of 106–138 °C, a 32 °C range versus 18 °C for the commercial film. Line trials on a production VFFS machine confirmed seal integrity of filled pouches under 1.5 bar air pressure.

sources.value: The project investigated the relationship between seal-layer formulation variables—resin type, comonomer content, blend ratios, and film thickness—and the achievable thermal processing window on VFFS packaging lines running at up to 300 bags/min. Work was conducted across four tasks: rheological and thermal characterisation of candidate resins; cast-film extrusion trials on the laboratory line at the Faculty of Technology; heat-seal testing using a gradient sealer and a laboratory VFFS unit; and statistical modelling of composition–property relationships using RSM. The project produced seven publications and validated two target formulations with an industrial partner. A trained PhD student and two master's students were involved. Equipment procured under the project included an updated hot-tack tester and an ATR-FTIR accessory.

Two standard seal-quality tests—the 180° peel test and the differential pressure burst test—were applied to heat-sealed pouches made from OPP/tie/mLLDPE films sealed across a jaw temperature range of 95–140 °C. For each jaw temperature, 20 pouches were prepared and tested by both methods. Peel force data and burst pressure data were analysed for correlation and for their ability to discriminate between adequate and inadequate seals. The two methods agreed in classifying seals above 110 °C as acceptable (peel ≥ 25 N/25 mm; burst ≥ 180 kPa), but diverged in the 100–109 °C zone, where 7 of 20 pouches passed the burst test but failed the peel criterion. Root-cause analysis by SEM cross-section showed incomplete interdiffusion at the seal interface in those pouches. Repeatability expressed as coefficient of variation was 5.8 % for peel and 9.2 % for burst across all jaw temperatures. The peel test is recommended as the more conservative acceptance criterion for VFFS applications handling liquid or particulate products.

Three-layer films with an oriented polypropylene (OPP) structural layer, an adhesive tie layer, and an mLLDPE seal layer were produced by lamination. Seal-layer thickness was varied at 10, 15, 20, 25 and 30 µm while total film gauge was held at 60 µm. Sealing experiments were conducted on a laboratory gradient heat-sealer over a 85–140 °C jaw temperature range; dwell time was fixed at 0.4 s and jaw pressure at 0.25 N/mm². Seal strength and hot-tack force were measured. Films with 20 µm seal layers achieved plateau seal strength of 31 N/25 mm and maintained hot-tack force above 6 N/25 mm over a 28 °C window (108–136 °C). Reducing the seal layer to 10 µm narrowed the hot-tack window to 16 °C and lowered plateau seal strength to 22 N/25 mm; increasing to 30 µm provided no significant benefit. Optical microscopy of cross-sections confirmed nominal thicknesses within ±1.5 µm. The 20 µm seal layer is proposed as the practical optimum for this film construction.

Seal-initiation temperature (SIT) is a primary determinant of packaging line throughput on vertical form–fill–seal machines. This work compared cast films produced from four mLLDPE resins differing in comonomer type (1-butene, 1-hexene, or 1-octene) at constant density (0.918 g/cm³) and melt flow index (2.0 g/10 min). Films of 40 µm nominal thickness were extruded on a laboratory cast-film line and sealed over a 90–135 °C range at 0.3 N/mm² and 0.5 s dwell time. Seal strength was measured by 180° peel on a tensile tester. The 1-octene grade yielded the lowest SIT (97 °C) and a plateau seal strength of 28 N/25 mm, compared to 108 °C and 22 N/25 mm for the 1-butene grade. DSC melting profiles correlated well with the observed SIT differences. Hot-tack measurements at 500 mm/s jaw separation confirmed that 1-octene resins provide a 14 °C wider hot-tack window, relevant for high-speed filling lines.

A two-dimensional finite-difference model was developed to simulate transient heat and moisture transfer in a sealed steel enclosure containing a heat-dissipating printed circuit board. The model couples Fourier conduction through the walls with Fickian vapour diffusion and accounts for condensation on internal surfaces when local temperature drops below the dew point. Internal heat generation was set at 5 W, representing a typical low-power controller unit. Simulations were run for a 24-hour diurnal ambient profile representative of a Pannonian autumn day. Results showed that condensation first occurred on the lower half of the front panel after approximately 17 minutes of rapid external temperature drop at −1.2 °C/min. Increasing the initial internal air volume by 30 % by deepening the enclosure reduced condensation onset time by only 4 minutes, while adding a 2-g silica-gel desiccant delayed onset by 38 minutes. The model was validated against thermocouple and humidity logger measurements from a physical enclosure subjected to a controlled temperature ramp in a climate chamber.

sources.value: Fourteen silicone O-rings were removed from photovoltaic string combiner boxes that had been in service for approximately five years at three sites across Vojvodina. Visual inspection, Shore A hardness testing, tensile testing, thermogravimetric analysis, and SEM imaging were performed on extracted seals and compared with unused reference samples from the same production lot. Average hardness increased by 9 Shore A units, elongation at break decreased by 31 %, and TGA showed a 2.1 % mass loss in the 200–400 °C range attributed to low-molecular-weight siloxane volatilisation. SEM images revealed surface crazing on seals from south-facing installations, consistent with UV-ozone degradation. Correlation analysis showed that enclosures with measured internal humidity above 75 % RH for more than 400 cumulative hours per year had a significantly higher incidence of corrosion on copper busbars, linking seal degradation to electrical component failure.

sources.value: MOISTMOD targets the development of validated computational models for predicting moisture accumulation and condensation onset in sealed outdoor enclosures used in low-voltage electrical distribution infrastructure. The project combines laboratory climate-chamber experiments with two-dimensional coupled heat-moisture FEM simulations. A parametric study covering five enclosure sizes, three gasket materials, and four regional climate profiles is being conducted. An open-access Python-based tool for condensation-onset prediction is under development. The project involves collaboration with a meteorological data provider and an enclosure manufacturer. One postdoctoral researcher and two doctoral students are supported under the project.

The project set up a networked outdoor test rack with 24 instrumented enclosures across three sites in Vojvodina to collect simultaneous internal humidity, temperature, and condensation-event data over 30 months. Gasket specimens from each enclosure were retrieved at 10-month intervals for laboratory characterisation. The data collected formed the basis for the regression model relating enclosure configuration and gland fill ratio to condensation frequency, and provided field-correlation reference points for the accelerated ageing protocol developed subsequently. Two M.Sc. theses and one Ph.D. thesis were completed within the project scope.

NBR gaskets of two hardness grades (50 and 70 Shore A) were subjected to repeated immersion in distilled water at 25 °C for 8 hours followed by drying at 60 °C for 16 hours, simulating dew-cycle condensation, for up to 90 cycles. Mass uptake, dimensional change in thickness, and compression-set were tracked after every 15 cycles. The softer 50 Shore A grade reached a water uptake plateau of 4.8 % by mass after 45 cycles, accompanied by a 1.7 % thickness increase. The 70 Shore A grade showed 2.9 % uptake and 0.9 % thickness increase. Compressive stress relaxation tests after the final cycle showed that both grades lost 22–27 % of initial contact-force capacity. Hardness measurements after cycling indicated slight softening (−3 to −5 Shore A units) for both grades. The data suggest that groove-depth tolerances should be re-evaluated when NBR seals are used in condensation-prone environments.

sources.value: Six aluminium flange specimens were machined to surface roughness values Ra between 0.8 µm and 6.3 µm, and paired with 2-mm NBR and EPDM flat gaskets at clamping pressures of 1, 2, and 4 MPa. Helium leak tests were conducted at an internal overpressure of 0.5 bar. Leak rate increased by more than one order of magnitude when Ra changed from 1.6 µm to 6.3 µm at the lowest clamping pressure. At 4 MPa clamping, NBR showed a 40 % lower leak rate than EPDM on rougher surfaces, attributed to its higher elastic modulus enabling better micro-asperity conformity at elevated contact stress. A contact-mechanics model based on Greenwood–Williamson statistics was used to predict effective contact area and showed reasonable agreement with measured leak rates. Practical guidelines for flange finishing standards in low-preload enclosure assemblies are proposed.

The heat transfer coefficient (HTC) between polymer melt and mould steel during the filling and packing stages is a poorly characterised boundary condition that strongly influences warpage predictions. This study systematically varied the interfacial HTC from 1000 to 10 000 W/m²K in a commercial process simulation environment for a PA6 box-shaped part (80 × 60 × 30 mm, 2.5 mm wall) and quantified the resulting spread in predicted warpage and residual stress distributions. Warpage at the open rim varied by up to 0.38 mm (factor of 2.4) over the HTC range, whereas residual stresses at mid-wall varied by less than 6%. An inverse identification procedure using CMM warpage measurements from 20 experimental parts at two mould temperatures was used to back-calculate effective HTC values. Identified HTC values were 2 400 ± 310 W/m²K at 40 °C mould temperature and 1 850 ± 260 W/m²K at 70 °C mould temperature. Recommendations for standardising HTC calibration in simulation workflows are given.

sources.value: This study examines how packing pressure level affects the degree of crystallinity distribution and final part warpage in polyamide 6 (PA6) flat components (100 × 100 × 2 mm). Experiments were performed on a 60-tonne hydraulic injection moulding machine at packing pressures ranging from 40 to 100 MPa in steps of 20 MPa. Crystallinity was measured by DSC on specimens cut from five through-thickness positions. Warpage was quantified with a coordinate measuring machine at a 5 × 5 grid of points. Higher packing pressure increased average crystallinity from 28% to 36% but reduced warpage from 0.41 mm to 0.17 mm due to reduced volumetric shrinkage. A commercial process simulation code was used to model the crystallisation kinetics using an Avrami-type model with parameters fitted to the DSC data. Simulated crystallinity gradients matched measured gradients with a mean absolute error of 2.3 percentage points across all packing conditions.

Thick-walled PP optical mounting brackets (nominal wall thickness 8 mm) for automotive lighting assemblies require tight dimensional tolerances and are particularly susceptible to warpage driven by differential cooling between the cavity and core sides of the mould. This study investigates the relationship between the cooling rate asymmetry and final warpage for four mould configurations with varying cavity-to-core mould temperature ratios (ΔT = 0, 10, 20, 30 °C; cavity side always colder). Warpage was measured on 15 parts per condition using a structured-light scanner with 0.02 mm point accuracy. Differential cooling induced a systematic bowing, with warpage increasing from 0.12 mm at ΔT = 0 to 0.91 mm at ΔT = 30 °C. Thermomechanical simulations captured this trend with a maximum error of 0.11 mm. Through-thickness crystallinity measurements confirmed that the core-side crystallinity exceeded the cavity-side value by up to 6 percentage points at ΔT = 30 °C, directly contributing to differential shrinkage.

sources.value: Aleksandar Bošković received his Dipl.Ing. degree in Mechanical Engineering from the University of Novi Sad in 2004 and his PhD from the same institution in 2011, with a thesis on residual stress formation in injection-moulded semi-crystalline thermoplastics. He was appointed Assistant Professor in 2012 and promoted to Associate Professor in 2018 within the Department of Mechanical Engineering at the Faculty of Technical Sciences. His research group focuses on coupled thermomechanical simulation of polymer processing, particularly predicting warpage, residual stresses, and optimising mould cooling systems for semi-crystalline materials such as polyamide and polypropylene. He teaches courses in Machine Elements and Polymer Processing Technology. The group works primarily with commercial FEA and injection moulding simulation packages, and has access to a materials testing laboratory with DSC, tensile testing frames, and coordinate measuring equipment for warpage validation.

Two-component injection moulding of polypropylene (PP) substrate and polyamide 6 (PA6) overmould was studied with respect to residual stress development and warpage. The process involves sequential injection into a rotary mould; the PP substrate cools partially before PA6 is injected over it. A sequential thermomechanical FE simulation was implemented to capture stress accumulation in both materials and at the interface. The PP thermoviscoelastic material model and PA6 crystallisation model were taken from previous calibrated studies. Simulations were compared against CMM warpage measurements on 40 two-component plaques (160 × 80 mm) produced at two substrate pre-cooling times (8 and 15 s). Predicted warpage matched measurements within 0.09 mm for the 15 s pre-cooling case and within 0.21 mm for the 8 s case, where incomplete solidification of the substrate introduced additional uncertainty. Interfacial stress concentrations are identified as a potential delamination risk at sharp edges.

PERMTEMP aimed to produce a systematically collected reference dataset of temperature-dependent oxygen, carbon dioxide and water vapour permeability for ten commercially relevant polyolefin film grades, covering the range 5–50 °C. Arrhenius activation energies and pre-exponential factors were determined by least-squares regression on multi-temperature OTR and WVTR datasets. The dataset was made available to Serbian food-industry companies through a technical report and an online spreadsheet tool for shelf-life estimation. The project also calibrated the Faculty of Technology permeability laboratory instruments against certified reference films, establishing a documented calibration protocol that remains in use.

Commercially metallised cast polypropylene (CPP) films with aluminium optical densities ranging from 2.1 to 3.6 were characterised for OTR and WVTR immediately after production and after 90-day ambient storage. At optical density 3.6, OTR was 4 cm³/(m²·day·bar) and WVTR was 0.18 g/(m²·day) immediately after metallisation. After 90 days these rose by 18 % and 24 % respectively. SEM cross-sections and atomic force microscopy revealed microcrack formation in the aluminium layer, with crack density correlating with ageing-induced OTR increase (R² = 0.87). Corona pre-treatment level (measured by contact angle) did not significantly affect initial barrier but reduced the rate of crack formation during ageing by approximately 30 %. The study provides quantitative ageing coefficients applicable to worst-case shelf-life calculations for hermetically sealed snack products.

She joined the Department of Materials Engineering as an assistant professor in 2008 and was promoted to full professor in 2019. Her research group focuses on the transport properties of polyolefin-based multilayer and mono-material packaging films, with particular attention to oxygen and water vapour transmission rates across temperature gradients, crystallinity effects, and the design of EVOH-free high-barrier systems compatible with mechanical recycling streams. She teaches courses in Polymer Materials and Packaging Technology. Biaxially oriented polypropylene (BOPP) films prepared at draw ratios of 5×5 to 9×9 were characterised for oxygen transmission rate (OTR) using a coulometric sensor method at 23 °C and 0 % relative humidity. Wide-angle X-ray scattering confirmed an increase in crystallinity from 42 % to 61 % with rising draw ratio. OTR values decreased from 1840 to 890 cm³/(m²·day·bar) over the same range. DSC measurements showed that lamellar thickness, as estimated by the Thomson–Gibbs equation, increased from 8.2 to 14.7 nm. A linear correlation was established between the reciprocal of lamellar thickness and OTR, consistent with a tortuous-path diffusion model. FTIR-ATR band ratios at 998/973 cm⁻¹ were used as an independent crystallinity index and agreed within 4 % with WAXS results. The findings provide quantitative guidance for process optimisation of BOPP films where oxygen barrier is the primary constraint.

A dataset of 214 production batches of three-layer LLDPE/mLLDPE/LLDPE cast films (40–80 µm) collected over 18 months from an industrial film producer was analysed to establish a statistical relationship between pinhole density (measured by electrical discharge imaging) and OTR. Pinhole density ranged from 0 to 8 pinholes/m² and OTR ranged from 1600 to 3100 cm³/(m²·day·bar). A linear regression model explained 61 % of OTR variance (R² = 0.61) using pinhole density as the sole predictor; inclusion of film thickness, extrusion speed and melt temperature raised R² to 0.79. Films with zero pinholes showed an OTR range of 1580–1980 cm³/(m²·day·bar), confirming that pinhole-free conditions alone do not guarantee low OTR. These findings are communicated to the production partner as a quality-control decision tool. The methodology is generic and applicable to other thin film geometries.

A two-dimensional finite-volume model of moisture and heat transport was developed for a generic polycarbonate housing representative of handheld electronic devices. The domain included the polymer shell, an internal air cavity of 38 cm³, and a printed circuit board heat source. Boundary conditions followed a 24-hour ambient cycle between 5 °C and 35 °C at 60–90 % relative humidity, representative of coastal storage conditions. The dew-point margin at the coldest internal surface was tracked over 72 simulated hours. For a housing wall thickness of 2 mm with no desiccant, the dew-point margin dropped below zero during the cooling phase at hour 14, predicting condensation on the board. Adding a 0.5 g silica gel insert raised the margin to +1.8 °C at the same instant. Model sensitivity to polycarbonate vapour diffusivity was assessed over a ±30 % range; the condensation-onset time varied by ±2.1 hours. The numerical approach is validated against laboratory cycling tests using thermocouples and a miniature humidity probe placed inside the cavity.

sources.value: A coupled simulation workflow was developed to map condensation risk on internal surfaces of wall-mounted outdoor plastic housings under winter conditions. A three-dimensional steady-state CFD model computed the internal temperature distribution accounting for natural convection and wall conduction; the resulting surface temperature field was then passed as a boundary condition to a vapour diffusion model that predicted local relative humidity and dew-point margin at each surface node. A 6-litre ABS housing with a 20 W internal heat source was simulated at external temperatures of −10 °C, 0 °C, and 10 °C at 90 % external relative humidity with a seal permeance of 3.5 × 10⁻¹² kg/(m²·s·Pa). At −10 °C, 14 % of the internal wall area showed a negative dew-point margin; this reduced to 3 % at 0 °C and to zero at 10 °C. A redesign placing the heat source at the geometric bottom of the housing eliminated the negative-margin area at −10 °C. The workflow is implemented in open-source tools and requires less than 4 hours of computation time on a workstation.

sources.value: This project developed a prototype wireless sensor node small enough to be enclosed permanently inside a standard IP65 cabinet, transmitting temperature and humidity readings via LoRaWAN. Sabo's group led the work package on enclosure climate modelling and sensor placement optimisation, using CFD and hygrothermal simulations to identify locations within the cabinet where the sensor reading is most representative of the condensation-risk state of the enclosure. Two candidate sensor positions were evaluated against a 24-thermocouple reference dataset; the recommended position reduced the root-mean-square error in condensation-onset prediction from 4.1 hours to 1.3 hours compared with an unguided placement. The project partnered with an electronics engineering group for sensor hardware and firmware development.

Twelve steel electrical cabinets installed in four unheated substations in Vojvodina were instrumented with internal and external temperature–humidity loggers over a 14-month period spanning two winters. Internal relative humidity exceeded 85 % for more than 480 hours per year in cabinets without anti-condensation heaters, with the longest continuous exceedance episode lasting 61 hours. A lumped-parameter hygrothermal model driven by measured exterior boundary conditions reproduced the measured internal humidity with a root-mean-square error of 3.2 percentage points. Model calibration identified the dominant vapour pathway as the cable entry glands rather than the door gasket, accounting for approximately 68 % of total vapour ingress. Anti-condensation heater power requirements derived from the model range from 6 W to 22 W depending on cabinet volume. Recommendations for gland specification and heater sizing are given.

This book chapter reviews the physical mechanisms governing moisture behaviour in mechanically sealed enclosures, covering vapour diffusion through seal materials, convective moisture transport in internal air volumes, and sorption on interior polymer surfaces. The chapter presents one-dimensional and two-dimensional analytical solutions for steady-state and transient vapour transport in simple geometries, followed by a discussion of finite-element and finite-volume implementations for complex enclosure shapes. A worked example demonstrates the prediction of condensation onset time for a 2-litre aluminium housing sealed with a silicone gasket subjected to a step change in external relative humidity from 50 % to 95 %. The chapter also addresses the coupling between thermal and hygric calculations, noting conditions under which decoupled analysis is acceptable (Biot number for vapour transfer below 0.1). Measurement techniques for validating hygrothermal models, including gravimetric permeability testing, capacitive sensing, and fibre-optic dew-point measurement, are described.

sources.value: A hygrothermal model of a polyphthalamide (PPA) junction box used in crystalline silicon photovoltaic modules was subjected to a global sensitivity analysis using the Sobol variance decomposition method. Nine input parameters were varied: gasket vapour permeability, gasket cross-section width, groove surface roughness, internal air volume, internal polymer sorption isotherm slope, external temperature amplitude, external humidity amplitude, solar irradiance-driven temperature offset, and potting compound surface area. Each parameter was sampled over physically realistic ranges drawn from the literature and from in-house measurements. A total of 18 432 model evaluations were performed. The first-order Sobol index for the time to condensation onset was dominated by gasket vapour permeability (S₁ = 0.41) and external humidity amplitude (S₁ = 0.28). Grove surface roughness had a smaller but non-negligible contribution (S₁ = 0.09). The analysis identifies gasket material selection and installation surface finish as the most impactful design levers for extending the condensation-free service life of PV junction boxes.

sources.value: A simulation workflow is described that takes hourly meteorological station data (dry-bulb temperature and relative humidity) as its sole external boundary condition and predicts the time-history of the dew-point margin on the coldest internal surface of a sealed outdoor enclosure. The workflow chains a thermal resistance–capacitance model of the enclosure wall with a lumped vapour mass-balance model and a local surface temperature correction derived from a short CFD pre-computation. It was applied to three years of hourly data (2021–2023) from the Rimski Šančevi meteorological station near Novi Sad for three enclosure configurations: unheated ABS 1-litre, unheated aluminium 4-litre, and aluminium 4-litre with 10 W anti-condensation heater. The workflow predicted that the unheated ABS enclosure experienced 312 condensation-onset events over three years; the unheated aluminium enclosure experienced 94, and the heated aluminium enclosure experienced zero. Predictions were validated against a 12-month data set from four instrumented enclosures deployed at the same station, with onset event counts matching to within 8 %.

sources.value: Optical devices assembled in factories at relative humidity levels of 30 %, 50 %, and 70 % were modelled and tested to quantify the long-term internal moisture level reached after hermetic sealing. A one-dimensional mass-balance model predicts that the asymptotic internal humidity is determined by the initial air charge, the internal surface sorption capacity of polymer components, and the slow permeation through glass-to-metal adhesive joints. For an assembly humidity of 70 %, the model predicts a post-sealing equilibrium internal relative humidity of 22 % at 20 °C; at 30 % assembly humidity this falls to 9 %. Twelve laboratory assemblies per condition, sealed with a tin-indium solder alloy joint, were placed in a climate chamber and monitored via a fibre-optic dew-point sensor for 18 months. Predictions and measurements agree within 4 percentage points. The study underpins a factory specification of maximum 45 % assembly-room humidity to maintain the internal level below 15 % over a 10-year service life.

sources.value: Vapour permeability was measured for EPDM, silicone, and thermoplastic polyurethane (TPU) seal materials in unaged condition and after accelerated thermal ageing (100 °C, 1000 hours) and UV ageing (1.0 W/m² at 340 nm, 500 hours) in accordance with ISO 4892-2. Gravimetric cup tests at 23 °C and 85 % relative humidity differential were conducted on three specimens per material per ageing condition. EPDM permeability increased by 12 % after thermal ageing and by 8 % after UV ageing relative to the unaged baseline. Silicone showed no statistically significant change after thermal ageing but a 19 % increase after UV ageing. TPU exhibited the largest sensitivity, with permeability increasing by 34 % after thermal ageing and 27 % after UV ageing, accompanied by visible surface crazing and a 15 % reduction in hardness. Shore A hardness, tensile elongation at break, and infrared spectroscopy were used to characterise degradation mechanisms. The results indicate that TPU is not recommended for long-service-life outdoor enclosures exposed to solar radiation.

A central composite design was used to map the effect of barrel temperature (120–160 °C), screw speed (80–200 rpm), and sunflower protein concentrate content (0–25 wt%) on the mechanical and barrier properties of blown films produced from the extruded blends via a subsequent film blowing step. Seventeen experimental runs yielded response surfaces for tensile strength, elongation at break, Young's modulus, water vapour transmission rate (WVTR), and oxygen transmission rate (OTR). Tensile strength ranged from 7.2 to 16.8 MPa across the design space; OTR varied from 180 to 620 cm³·m⁻²·day⁻¹·bar⁻¹. Optimal conditions identified by desirability function (maximum strength and minimum OTR) were 148 °C, 145 rpm, and 18 wt% protein. At the optimum, predicted and experimental values agreed within 6%. Specific mechanical energy was modelled as a secondary response and found to increase linearly with screw speed but to show a quadratic relationship with protein content, with a minimum near 12 wt% attributed to lubrication effects of denatured protein at low concentration.

Polyetherimide (PEI) is used in precision-fit diagnostic device components where dimensional tolerances of ±0.02 mm or tighter are required. This work tracks dimensional changes in injection-moulded PEI discs and pins stored in sealed packaging at three relative humidity levels (30%, 60%, and 90%) over 18 months. CMM measurements at six-month intervals show that at 90% RH, average diameter growth reached 0.015 mm after 18 months, representing 75% of the maximum allowable tolerance. Moisture uptake at 90% RH reached 1.2 wt%, consistent with literature values for unfilled PEI. Specimens stored at 30% RH showed negligible dimensional change (<0.003 mm). A linear predictive model relating absorbed moisture to dimensional deviation, validated against independent specimens, is presented with 95% confidence intervals. The study provides evidence to support the use of desiccant packaging with a humidity indicator below 40% RH for long shelf-life storage of PEI diagnostic components.

sources.value: Selective laser sintered (SLS) polyamide 12 specimens were subjected to 10 repeated cycles of moisture absorption (95% RH, 37 °C, 7 days) and desorption (23 °C, 50% RH, 7 days) prior to fatigue testing. A control group was tested in the dry-as-built condition. Tension–tension fatigue tests (R = 0.1, 1 Hz, 37 °C) were performed. The cyclic hygroscopic treatment reduced fatigue life at 40 MPa by 38% compared with the dry control group. Micro-CT imaging performed before and after the hygroscopic cycling revealed enlargement of interlayer porosity, with mean pore diameter increasing from 48 µm to 67 µm. Dynamic mechanical analysis (DMA) showed a reduction in storage modulus of 12% and an increase in the loss tangent peak area of 18% after hygroscopic cycling, indicating increased viscoelastic energy dissipation per cycle. The findings are relevant to the growing use of SLS-printed PA12 in patient-specific surgical guides and low-load orthopaedic ancillaries.

sources.value: Three accelerated ageing protocols for thermoplastic polyurethane (TPU) catheter tubing segments are compared: elevated temperature immersion (70 °C in phosphate-buffered saline), combined UV/humidity exposure (UVA, 0.76 W/m², 50% RH), and real-time ageing at 23 °C/50% RH over 52 weeks. Fatigue life under cyclic bending (displacement-controlled, 1 Hz, 180° bend radius) was measured for each protocol at nominal ageing equivalents of 6, 12, 24, and 52 weeks. The elevated temperature protocol was the most aggressive: fatigue life after 24-week equivalent ageing dropped to 42% of the initial value. Molecular weight (GPC), hardness (Shore A), and elongation at break were measured alongside fatigue data. Arrhenius correlation between the 70 °C and 23 °C datasets yielded an activation energy of 84 kJ/mol, within the range expected for hydrolytic degradation of polyester-based TPU. The UV/humidity protocol produced divergent results not predictable from the thermal model, suggesting a different degradation mechanism relevant only to external device surfaces.

sources.value: This paper investigates whether DMA measurements—specifically storage modulus E′, loss modulus E″, and the loss tangent tan δ recorded at 1, 10, and 100 Hz—can serve as rapid non-destructive predictors of residual fatigue life in humidity-aged polymer specimens without performing full fatigue tests. Four materials were studied: PA6, PA66-GF30, POM-C, and PEEK, each aged at 85% RH and 37 °C for 0, 4, 8, 16, and 32 weeks. DMA signatures were correlated with fatigue lives measured at a fixed stress amplitude of 40% of the tensile strength for each material–ageing combination (n = 8 per data point). For PA6 and PA66-GF30, tan δ at 1 Hz showed the strongest correlation with residual fatigue life (Pearson r = −0.91 and −0.87 respectively). POM-C and PEEK showed weaker correlations (r = −0.61 and −0.54), consistent with their low moisture uptake limiting the DMA-detectable change. A simple regression-based screening criterion using tan δ thresholds is proposed and its applicability limits are discussed.

value.text: Raspberries for Germany arrive with mould on day 9; buyers want 14 days.
value.detail: We ship raspberries from Serbian packing houses to buyers in Germany and the Netherlands. The berries leave Serbia in good condition — our own quality checks confirm that — but by day nine of a typical fourteen-day shelf-life window, a meaningful share of punnets show visible Botrytis mould. Buyers have started issuing penalty deductions and two accounts have threatened to switch suppliers unless we fix this before next season, which means we have roughly eight months. The punnet itself is a standard 125 g rPET shell with a heat-sealed anti-fog lidding film. We have run informal trials with two different film grades and adjusted seal pressures, but mould rates did not drop enough to matter. We suspect the issue is a combination of micro-condensation inside the punnet and an oxygen-transmission rate that is not well matched to berry respiration at 2–4 °C. We have OTR and CO₂TR instruments in the lab and can measure headspace gas composition, but we do not have the modelling background to translate those numbers into a film specification. We also have real shipment data — temperature logs, humidity logs, and destination inspection reports — from the last two seasons. Budget for trials is limited; we can fund materials and lab time but cannot afford a large external testing programme. A good result is punnets reaching day fourteen with mould incidence below one percent, confirmed in controlled simulated-transit tests.

FreshPak Solutions was set up in 2012 by two former food-logistics managers, Dragan Kovačević and Marta Ilić, who kept watching Serbian berry exporters lose shipments to bad packaging. We started with a single thermoforming line in a rented hall and a list of about a dozen growers in the Fruška Gora corridor. Twelve years later we have 60 people, three production lines, and a quality lab that runs seal-strength, permeability and drop tests every day. Most of what we make ends up under raspberries, blueberries and sour cherries heading to Germany, Austria and the Netherlands. Our direct customers are packing houses and export cooperatives; we work closely with their agronomists and logistics teams to match packaging spec to cold-chain conditions. What separates us from the large Western suppliers is response time and willingness to run short customised batches. A grower can call on a Tuesday and have trial punnets by Friday. We are not the cheapest, but our reject rate at destination is consistently below two percent, which is what keeps buyers coming back. The next step for us is moving the whole lidding-film range to certified compostable materials before the retail mandates kick in.

value.bio: Jelena Marković is a Full Professor at the University of Novi Sad's Faculty of Technology, Department of Food Preservation Engineering. Her research integrates food engineering, packaging science, and predictive microbiology to extend the shelf life of perishable horticultural products, with a particular focus on Serbian soft fruits. She has extensive experience developing modified atmosphere packaging systems and mathematical models for microbial growth kinetics in cold-chain logistics. Professor Marković has collaborated with multiple Serbian fruit exporters on industrial packaging trials and serves as an academic partner on the FRESHROUTE innovation project targeting cold-chain optimization for berry exports. She is actively open to industrial PhD supervision and joint research projects with industry.
